notes.decision: Rendered 'is intent in heart.' This is the qualitative form of ⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ (Crum 511b) — 'be intent, careful, attentive of heart.' Recurs in lines 16 and 18 with the same value. The phrase frames the heretical question: did God 'set his heart upon' (i.e., personally intend) the molding of human flesh?

Read as ⲧ-ⲟⲓⲛ-ⲡⲗⲁⲥ 'the molding-action,' parallel formation to ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ 'the dissolution' (in glossary). The ⲟ̄ⲓⲛ- prefix forms an action-noun on the Greek verb πλάσσειν. The whole kephalaion treats the πλάσμα (cf. ⲡⲡⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ ⲛ̄ⲧⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲣⲱⲙⲉ in glossary).

Translated 'concerning' on contextual grounds. The form is obscure — possibly a Lycopolitan compound serving as a topic-introducing preposition before ⲡⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ. Could alternatively be 'as for' or 'about.' Flagged for parallels.

Translated 'in which she is intertwined, being bound.' ⲭⲁⲗⲭ from glossary 'mingle, fashion together' — used here of the soul's entanglement in the chains. Feminine ⲥ̄- and ⲉⲥ- confirm the soul (ⲡⲉϩⲧⲩⲭⲏ in line 25) as the bound entity raised forth.

Translated 'examine to see' — taking ⲙⲟⲩⲍ as Lyc. variant of ⲙⲟⲩϣⲧ̄ 'examine, scrutinize' and ⲁⲛⲉⲩ as ⲁ-ⲛⲁⲩ 'to seeing/to look.' The apostolic injunction shifts attention away from the disciples' false inference toward direct examination of the archons. Confidence moderate.
ⲛ̄-ⲕⲉ-ⲥⲁⲡ 'another time, again.' Standard Coptic temporal adverbial. Marks the transition from the heretical proposition's first clause to its restatement.

Line 6 contains visible but contextually obscure text on either side of a mid-line leer. Possible readings: 'they were ___' (closing prior chapter) and 'of Adam they are' / 'they are powers' (opening new chapter). The leer almost certainly marks the chapter transition; lines 4-5 contain trailing material and the formal heading respectively. Marked as lacunae with partial text noted.
Translated 'pondered forth concerning them' — preserving the spatial-emanative ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' and the directional ⲁϫⲱⲟⲩⲟⲩ 'upon them.' The archons' deliberation directed onto Adam and Eve.

Translated 'the Exalted One' — substantival relative on ϫⲁⲥⲉ 'be high, exalted.' Preserves the active-verbal sense (one who is exalted) over the static 'the High One.' Recurs on this page (lines 5, 11) as the heavenly archetype whose image is imprinted upon the molded humanity.

Translated 'liken... in a likeness' — preserving the cognate construction (verb + cognate-object noun). The archons performed an act of likening but only at the level of likeness, not of truth. Standard Manichaean distinction between resemblance-by-image and resemblance-in-substance.

Translated 'in the form of the tree' — taking ⲁⲩ̄- as a phonetic/orthographic variant or reduction of ⲍⲛ̄ⲟⲩ- 'in a' or simply Lyc. preposition. ⲡⲥⲙⲁⲧ = 'the form, manner.' ⲡⲩⲏⲛ = Lyc. ⲡϣⲏⲛ 'tree.' The archons' fashioning of humanity is being compared to a tree-form, but the tree-form is itself only a likeness, not the truth.
Translated 'a great free woman' — beginning the parable comparing the molding of humanity to the famous noblewoman whose beauty draws all the noble suitors but who remains hidden in her palace.

Translated 'noble / nobility' — etymology uncertain, but the parallel with ⲉⲗⲉⲩⲑⲉⲣⲁ 'free' (line 14, 27) and the explicit ⲉⲩⲅⲉⲛⲏⲥ 'noble' (line 22) and the ranks of dignity (ⲁⲝⲓⲱⲙⲁⲧⲓⲕⲏ, line 19) confirm a sense in the semantic field of nobility/glory. ⲱⲉⲩ may be a Lyc. variant related to ⲱⲩ 'great, magnificent.'
Analyzed as ⲥⲣ̄- (3sg.f. + ⲣ̄- 'do') + ⲡⲧⲕⲉⲟ 'the additional thing, moreover' (= ⲡϯⲕⲉⲟⲩⲁ?). Functions as 'she is moreover/also.' The noblewoman's beauty is added to her wealth and freedom.

Translated 'the fame' — Lyc. = Sah. ⲥⲟⲉⲓⲧ 'fame, report' (already in accumulated vocab as 'his fame/repute'). The fame of her beauty, like a missionary's fame, scatters forth (ⲥⲱⲣ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ) into every city.
Translated 'they desire continually' — taking ⲁⲛ as the iterative/continuative adverb 'again, continually,' modifying the desire of the noble suitors for the hidden lady's face.

Translated tentatively as 'laid bare/uncovered.' The verb is unidentified; context (parallel to 'no man has ever seen her' and following ⲡⲉⲥⲍⲟ ⲁⲧⲙⲉⲧ 'her face being shut') requires a verb of exposure or beholding. Possible Lyc reflexes considered: ⲗⲱⲣⲝ̄ 'be calm/decay,' ⲗⲱⲣⲕ̄ 'rest,' or a metathesized form. None fit decisively.

Translated tentatively 'commoners' (others of common station). ⲕⲉ- 'and other' + ⲃⲁⲩⲟⲛⲉ unidentified. Possibly Greek-derived (βάναυσοι 'mechanics, common workers' or κοινοί 'common'). Listed in proposed_terms.

Translated 'her fire' = her radiance. ⲥⲁⲧⲉ = Coptic 'fire, flame.' In context of revealing her face, the parallel 'her face and her fire' refers to her bodily radiance — fitting the Manichaean register where the Third Ambassador's revelation is figured as fiery splendor.

Translated 'before all the powers' rather than 'against all the powers.' ⲟⲩⲃⲉ in this context is locative-confrontational ('in face of, in front of') consistent with the Ambassador's open manifestation, not adversarial. The next clause clarifies that the manifestation was NOT to make archons depict his form — so 'before' fits the cosmic-display sense.

Translated 'redeem him forth' from ⲥⲱⲧⲉ 'redeem' (with Lyc orthography). The triplet ⲧⲟⲩⲱ (raise) / ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ (release) / ⲥⲱⲧⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ (redeem forth) preserves the directional-soteriological grammar mandated by the terminology rules.

Restored tentatively as 'Know also' with low confidence. The bracketed letters could equally support 'Hear also' or 'Consider also' — some imperative-discourse marker introducing a new exposition. The preserved -ⲉ does not uniquely identify the verb.

Translated 'established them' from Lyc ⲧⲁϩⲟⲩ (= Sah. ⲧⲁϩⲟ⸗ⲟⲩ 'set/place them'). Distinct from ⲧⲁⲩⲟ 'send forth' or ⲧⲁⲃⲟ in the sense 'cause to perish.' Context (fashioning Adam-Eve in the divine image) confirms 'establish.'

Parsed as indefinite article ⲁⲩ- (Lyc variant of ⲟⲩ-) + ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'divinity, godhead' = '(it is) a divinity.' The construction follows ⲧⲍⲉ ⲍⲱϩ ⲁⲛ ⲧⲉ ⲧⲉⲓ̈ 'thus also is this' which expects a predicate noun. The referent is the Most High (ⲡⲡⲉⲧⲭⲁⲥⲉ) whose image was imprinted upon Adam-Eve — he himself being a great divinity with retinue of powers and angels.

Translated 'lust' / 'concupiscence.' Reduplicated noun, evidently synonymous with ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ which appears in immediate parallel (lines 3-4). The doubled root suggests intensive sensual desire. New term proposed.

Translated 'his female.' Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡⲉϥ-ⲥϩⲓⲙⲉ 'his woman/wife' with metathesis ⲥϩⲓⲙⲉ → ⲥⲙⲉⲓⲉ. The male/female archonic pairing fits the Manichaean seduction-of-archons myth and the explicit mention of Adam and Eve in line 17.
Translated 'they were stripped bare.' From ⲃⲱϣ 'be naked, be stripped.' The progression ⲗⲱⲃϣ (mingled) → ⲃⲱϣ (stripped) → ⲕⲱϩ (burned) traces the descent into sensual seduction.
Translated 'they took/received.' Lycopolitan ⲝⲓ = Sahidic ϫⲓ 'take, receive.' Recurs three times on this page (lines 8, 11, 15) consistently for the archons receiving/taking a seal from the icon.
Translated 'seal' (already in glossary). Here the act of impressing the icon's likeness onto the archonic offspring — the seal-imprint by which Adam and Eve are formed in the icon's likeness.
Translated 'place by place.' Distributive construction, repeating the noun for distributive sense — standard Coptic.

Translated 'they begat her.' Lycopolitan ⲝⲡⲟ = Sahidic ϫⲡⲟ 'beget' with 3sg.f. object suffix -ⲥ. Confirmed by parallel ⲡⲭⲡⲟ ⲛ̄ⲧⲥⲩⲛⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ 'the begetting of intercourse' in line 21 (alternate spelling ⲭⲡⲟ for ⲝⲡⲟ).
Mid-line break. The first paragraph ends with the descriptive 'lower place'; the second paragraph opens with the enumeration of moldings.
Translated 'these moldings.' ⲁⲓ̈- functions as plural demonstrative (Lyc. variant of ⲛⲁⲓ̈- 'these'). The preceding leer-break confirms the start of a new periodic clause.

Translated 'boundary of the sea.' ⲡⲣⲓⲅⲁⲥ likely a scribal/dialectal variant of Greek πέρας 'boundary' (cf. ⲡⲡⲓⲣⲁⲥ ⲛ̄ⲑⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ already in vocabulary). The cosmological motif of the Father of Life setting the sea's boundary is well-attested.

Translated 'her fire ... her enthumesis.' ⲧⲉϩ- is the Lycopolitan feminine possessive 'her' (cf. ⲡⲉϩ- 'his' in glossary). The referent is the second molding (Matter/Hyle) personified as feminine — she fashions herself through her own fire and thought.
Mid-line break separating the description of Matter's self-fashioning from the formal naming of the second molding.

Translated 'the sea rose up at her feet.' ⲁⲥⲧⲉ likely a contracted/dialectal form of ⲁⲥⲧⲱⲕ ⲣⲁⲧⲉ ⲛⲉⲥ 'she stood fast on her feet' (cf. ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ in glossary). The sea (subject) rises to meet the fallen molding. Reading uncertain in detail but contextually clear.

Translated 'image-painter' (= ζωγράφος, in glossary as ⲍⲱⲣⲁⲫⲉ etc.). Variant orthography ϩ for ⲍ. The Matter-figure becomes her own image-painter through her enthumesis — a direct echo of the cosmological doctrine of Matter as ⲧⲍⲱⲣⲡⲁⲫⲟⲥ in earlier kephalaia.
Translated 'the root of Death.' Matter's self-fashioned nature IS identified as the root from which Death arises — direct correspondential identification (not analogy).
Translated 'she cried out, saying.' The lacuna [ⲉⲥ . . ⲱϣ] suggests a verbal form ending in -ⲱϣ. Most likely ⲉⲥ-ⲱϣ 'crying out' or ⲉⲥ-(ⲣ̄)ⲱϣ 'shouting.' Followed by ⲭⲉ introducing direct speech.

Translated 'Maidenhood'. The compound is ⲙⲛⲧ- (abstract prefix) + ⲁϣⲣⲉ. The Lyc. ⲁϣⲣⲉ likely corresponds to ϣⲉⲉⲣⲉ 'daughter, girl' or to a youth-term. The phrase 'the great teaching of Maidenhood' likely refers to the cosmic instruction associated with the Virgin of Light, in whose service Adamas of Light is sent against Hyle. Could alternatively be 'youth/virginity'. Confidence moderate.
Parsed as ⲁϥ-ⲫⲃⲓⲟ-ⲥ 'he subdued/humbled her' per glossary entry ⲫⲃ̄ⲟ 'subdue, vanquish'. Subject is Adamas of Light; object 'her' is Hyle/the dragon-abortion.
Translated 'the north': ⲥⲁ- 'side' + ⲙ̄ϩⲓⲧ 'north'. Standard Coptic cosmographic term. The 'cisterns of the north' is a Manichaean cosmographic locus where the abortion-Hyle is bound.
Translated 'their cisterns'. The plural ϣⲉⲩⲉ likely reflects ϣⲏⲩ 'cisterns, wells, pits'. Alternative: 'shafts/depths'. Fits cosmographic context of binding Hyle in the dark depths.

Translated 'the Boastful one'. ϣⲟⲩϣⲟⲩ 'boast, glory, pride.' Substantival use designates the proud/arrogant cosmic adversary — likely the King of Darkness or the principal abortion. The Nature falls 'to' him in the cosmogonic narrative.
